newsitem.title: USA: Cooker comfortable with 1997 EPS estimate.
newsitem.headline: Cooker comfortable with 1997 EPS estimate.

text.p: Cooker Restaurant Corp President Phillip Pritchard said Friday he was comfortable with the First Call consensus estimate that the company will earn $0.87 a share for 1997.

Speaking at a Montgomery Securities Hospitality Conference, he also said he was comfortable with analysts' estimates for 1997 sales of $140 million. "We feel very comfortable with that range," he said.
The company earned $0.72 a share in 1996, up from $0.60 in 1995. The 20 percent increase was achieved despite increases in average shares outstanding. Its 1996 sales were $110.3 million.
Pritchard said Cooker currently operates 48 restaurants and plans to grow operating units by at least 25 percent in 1997.
Chief Financial Officer David Sevig told analysts at the conference that the company sees capital expenditures of about $30 million in 1997, half of which would come from internally generated funds.
